title: audit the France state-resolution contradiction: 71.10% vs 97.44%
question: Two agents measured the SAME population - France test rows that can resolve a state through FR_REGIONS - and got answers an order of magnitude apart. Agent A (D073) reports at most 1,204,739 of 1,694,445 France test rows = 71.10% resolvable, 28.90% provably unresolvable, using a maximal exact-match gazetteer and taking union bounds over the 14 FR_REGIONS keys. Agent B (D077) reports 2.5620% unresolvable / 97.4380% ceiling on the same input, apparently applying a looser criterion. This task is to settle it: state ONE resolution criterion precisely, apply it to the profile evidence, and report both prior figures under your criterion so the disagreement is explained rather than averaged away. Also report which French administrative tokens (regions vs departments) each source file actually uses, per source. This gates a real engineering decision: whether a fix to FR_REGIONS is worth making at all. Do NOT just pick one of the two numbers.
base_rules:
HARD CONSTRAINTS
- READ-ONLY on the dataset and on _upstream/. Never modify, move or delete them.
- Read ONLY the compact profile JSON files in analysis_out/profile/. They are small
  (575 KB each) because this machine has under 1 GB of free RAM. Do NOT open the raw
  *.tsv files under amazon_ml_2026_research/student_resource/dataset/ - a 480 MB scan
  was OOM-killed on this box and will kill you too.
- You MAY read _upstream/src/*.py to check what a dictionary actually does.
- You may write exactly two files: your deliverable .md, and a .json sidecar in
  analysis_out/findings/ holding the structured numbers.
- Never fetch anything from the network. The competition prohibits external data
  lookup, with immediate disqualification as the penalty.

EVIDENCE STANDARD
Every number you state must be traceable to a field in the profile JSON. If a field
you need was not collected, say so explicitly and mark the gap - do not estimate and
do not invent a plausible-looking figure. Distinguish clearly between what the data
shows and what you are inferring.
already_checked:
ALREADY CHECKED AND REFUTED - DO NOT REDO THIS WORK

REFUTED-1 "French postal codes are discarded by the pin guard." DEAD. No country in
  this dataset has a postal field. France dig5/row = 0.004 in test_s1 vs US 0.110;
  only 0.413% of France test_s1 rows contain a standalone 5-digit number. The US
  5-digit values are house numbers. Leave the pin guard alone.

REFUTED-2 "FR_REGIONS is too thin." NOT UPHELD as a dictionary-gap claim. Three
  separate audit tasks (D070, D071, D072) confirmed no missing region entries among
  the region tokens actually present. The live issue is DIFFERENT and is what you are
  assigned: source-2/3 France rows carry CITIES/DEPARTMENTS rather than region names,
  so state is simply absent for them. Adding dictionary entries would not fix it,
  because those tokens are not in the table's domain at all.

ALSO RULED OUT, do not re-derive:
- pin_eq is dead (0.0% of rows). alt_tset is dead (nalt 0.6-1.0%).
- France blocking caps are HEALTHY: 99.94% of 2,222,310 keys survive S1_MAXCAP=300.
- Address component order is NOT a problem - order-robustness was measured (D126,
  D127) and is fine.
- The inline-postcode city loss and the ligature deletion defect (Coeur/Foeur/Soeur ->
  ur) are both confirmed but negligible for scoring. Do not re-derive them.
- US_STATES, IN_STATES and FR_REGIONS mappings need NO dictionary expansion.
- ADDR_CANON_COMMON empty mappings and the France w/e/s differences were measured
  and are behaviourally harmless.

THE CONTRADICTION YOU ARE RESOLVING
  D073: 1,204,739 / 1,694,445 = 71.10% resolvable, 28.90% provably unresolvable.
  D077: 2.5620% unresolvable / 97.4380% ceiling.
  Same population, order-of-magnitude disagreement. The likely cause is the
  RESOLUTION CRITERION, not the data - one uses a maximal exact gazetteer with union
  bounds, the other a looser test.
  Known anchors you must reconcile against: France test rows total 1,694,445;
  test_source1 is 259,452 of those = 15.31%. The three modern regions present are
  hauts-de-france, nouvelle-aquitaine, pays-de-la-loire, all already mapped. The
  s1/s2/s3 split of administrative tokens is documented in D073 and D077 - read both
  deliverables before theorising.

HOW TO WIN THIS TASK
  - Read analysis_out/findings/D073_mine_FR_REGIONS_France.md and
    D077_mine_US_STATES_France.md in full FIRST. Do not reverse-engineer their
    numbers from scratch; identify the exact criterion each used.
  - Then state your own criterion in one sentence, in terms of what a token must
    match for a row to count as 'state resolved'.
  - Quote the normalize.py lines that decide state extraction so the criterion is
    tied to real code, not to intuition.
  - If the profile lacks the component structure needed to decide, say so plainly and
    report the ceiling you CAN defend, clearly labelled as a bound. A defensible
    bound beats a confident wrong number.
  - Finish with an explicit ENGINEERING VERDICT: is extending FR_REGIONS worth doing?
    One paragraph, and name the criterion you are reasoning under.
